title: Personnel of the Echols and Hampton bands; Tyree Glenn
summary: He names the men in Charlie Echols's band and in Hampton's, recalls that Hampton's book was head arrangements, and speaks of his friendship with Tyree Glenn.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: I see. Who were some of the musicians in that Lionel Hampton orchestra and who were some of those in the other orchestra that you performed in at that time?
Well, we had a fellow by the name of Andy Anderson played tenor and we had Leroy "Snake" White. I'm talking about the Echols band. They were
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

both from Cleveland. He was a trumpet player, in charge of the rehearsals and in charge of the band when Echols was in his dressing room and Don Byas was at that time with Eddie Barefield over in the Cotton Club along with Tyree Glenn, and of course when I was at the Cotton Club with Lionel Hampton we had one of the greats, a tenor, Herschel Evans. It was such a joy to hear him blow, he was great. You know, in later years, he gained fame with Count Basie and Lawrence Brown came out of California, too, to join Ellington. When I was there at that time, Lawrence Brown was already with Ellington, so --

I see. What of the Hampton orchestra, do you remember any of the personnel of that band, do you remember who did some of the arrangements for that band? That was before his big break with Benny Goodman.

I don't recall who arranged most of Hampton's arrangements. Most of it were head arrangements -- there was no music involved, all you do is section by section to start doing some riffs, pretty soon you put it all together, that's how "Hey-Baba-Rebop" came about from a riff thing. Because you know Lionel made that famous.
So you and Tyree Glenn were very close

Yes, we were very -- all through the years we always got together and although -- may he rest in peace -- he worked very hard and he took my place when I left Armstrong in later years which I'll bring up at a later interview, my days with Satchmo.
